messages:
Mia Chen: Quick security check — we plan to enable a Private Endpoint for customer-acct-42 in us-west-2. Two quick things: 1) For inbound, should we do IP allowlist on the NLB + security group, or rely on SG only? 2) For outbound, we must block telemetry to third-party services except a handful of approved IPs — do we implement that via SG egress, route table/NAT, or a transit-gateway firewall? Also: confirm logging redaction for PII before logs leave the VPC. PR: https://git.company/redwood/infra/pull/4523 CC: @Raj Patel :eyes:

Raj Patel: Defense in depth — I prefer NLB IP allowlist + SG rules. NLB (with NACLs) gives an early layer; SG enforces port-level rules. For inbound: allow 443 from NLB SG, and keep NLB listener restricted to whitelisted IPs if partner demands static IPs.

For egress: use route-table -> NAT so you can control outbound IPs at subnet level. Security group egress is useful for instances/tasks, but it's stateful and can be harder to audit at scale. If you have a Transit Gateway or firewall appliance, push egress rules there for central control.

Snippet (terraform-ish) for SG + NLB allowlist:
```hcl
resource "aws_lb" "private_ep" {
  load_balancer_type = "network"
  internal = true
  subnets = var.private_subnets
  enable_deletion_protection = true
}
resource "aws_security_group" "pe_sg" {
  ingress { from_port = 443 to_port = 443 protocol = "tcp" cidr_blocks = [aws_lb.private_ep.dns_name] }
}
```

Note: NLB IP allowlist can be done via AWS WAF IPSet on ALB/ALB-like layer or using NACLs if you need CIDR blocking.

Also: do not rely on SG egress to block all 3rd-party telemetry if workloads use managed networking (Fargate/Lambda) — prefer NAT + firewall.

Olivia Gomez: +1 to the approval flow note. If this endpoint is exposed to a partner, require an Access Portal request with justification and retention window. Approvals: security owners + legal sign-off for partner data. For logs: mask at source. Don't ship raw request bodies out. Use structured redaction and a denylist for PII fields (email, ssn, phone).

SecurityBot: Automated policy scan results for infra PR 4523:
- FAIL: log group `private-endpoint-usw2` has no redaction filter configured (policy INF-LOG-RED-03)
- WARN: NLB TLS listener not enforcing SNI validation (policy INF-TLS-01)
- INFO: no open ingress to 0.0.0.0/0 detected
See: https://policies.company/internal/scan/9482 :lock:

Mia Chen: Thanks. For redaction, can you suggest a minimal CloudWatch filter or agent config we can apply? We want regex-based masking before logs hit the group. Also need the exact list of approved telemetry IPs to add to the NAT allowlist.

Raj Patel: For CloudWatch fluent-bit config, do a filter like:
```yaml
[FILTER]
    Name    modify
    Match   private-*
    Regex_Working_Field  request_body  ("email":\"[^\"]+\"|"ssn":\"[^\"]+\")
    Replace_With  request_body  "<REDACTED>"
```
That masks common fields. We'll own the final regex set.

Approved telemetry endpoints (shortlist):
- 54.23.11.101 (metrics.vendor-a.com)
- 52.24.33.88 (logs.vendor-b.net)
I'll add the full list to the ticket.

DevOps Pager: I'll open a terraform PR to: add NLB WAF IPSet, tighten SGs, add route-table NAT egress deny-by-default + allowlist, and push a fluent-bit filter to the CloudWatch agent config. ETA: EOD tomorrow. PR link when ready. :hammer_and_wrench:

Olivia Gomez: Reminder: include acceptance criteria for security review — list of approved IPs, proof of redaction in staging logs (screenshot or sample), and Access Portal approval screenshot if partner access.

Mia Chen: Perfect. I'll update PR 4523 with acceptance checklist and attach staged logs once DevOps has the filter. Thanks all :pray:
